situation (example wording): "crime in Alameda County since 2018", "crime in Portland", "show crime in Pennsylvania", "new orleans"
what the app does today: A question that says "crime" (or names only a place) for a state, a county or a place with several agencies asks which kind of crime (P34, P118, D09); only one agency's "crime" by month is answered (P148).
proposed behavior: "Crime", "overall crime" or "all crimes" with no kind named is violent crime and property crime, for any place where that answer exists: built today as the two totals (the ask's "Both" button); the seven parts beside them (murder, rape, robbery, aggravated assault; burglary, larceny-theft, motor vehicle theft) come with the crime-over-time capability, from the Crime Index figures (Current Trends for months, the historical file for years). With a note: "No kind of crime was named, so violent crime and property crime are shown." The buttons offer one specific crime. A bare place name is the same question. P148's shape for one agency by month is unchanged. EXCEPTION (Jeff 2026-11-21): a clearance question (a clearance rate, offenses cleared, clearances by type) with no kind of crime named still asks which kind of crime; the violent-plus-property default does not apply to clearances ("clearance rates in Chicago", "Break down the exceptional clearances in Newark by type").
exact default or choices offered: Note and buttons: "Violent crime only", "Property crime only", "A specific crime" (which then asks which one).
why: Jeff 2026-11-21 (typed, through the coordinator): "Crime" with no kind named = violent crime and property crime with their parts, with a note and buttons for a specific crime. Supersedes the ask of P34, P118 and D09 (D09 stays for what the buttons offer).
